title: Right-Sizing and Reserved Capacity
description: Cut spend by matching SKUs to real utilisation, then commit only the steady-state floor.

data.text: The monthly Azure bill is $18,000 and finance wants it down 30% without hurting performance. The App Service plan runs at 12% average CPU across 6 instances, the SQL database is S3 with 700 DTU peak but 90 DTU average, and everything is pay-as-you-go.

Two independent levers. First **right-size**: 6 instances at 12% CPU is 4 instances too many, and S3 sized for a 700 DTU peak pays for idle capacity all month — move the database to a serverless or lower tier and let a scale-out handle peaks, or keep the peak tier but only during known windows. Second, **commit the steady-state floor** with a **reserved instance** or **savings plan** covering the minimum you run 24/7; never commit the burst.

data.title: Find the steady-state floor before committing
data.code:
// Azure Monitor metrics exported to Log Analytics:
// p05 of usage is your floor; p95 is your peak.
AzureMetrics
| where ResourceId has "app-quotient-prod"
| where MetricName == "CpuPercentage"
| summarize p05 = percentile(Average, 5),
            p50 = percentile(Average, 50),
            p95 = percentile(Average, 95)
          by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 30

data.title: Buy a reservation against the floor
data.code:
# Inspect what is eligible and how much is already covered
az consumption reservation summary list \
  --reservation-order-id <order-id> --grain-type daily

# 1-year reservation for the SQL steady-state, not the peak tier
az reservations reservation-order purchase \
  --reservation-order-id <order-id> \
  --sku "Standard_D4s_v3" \
  --location westeurope \
  --reserved-resource-type VirtualMachines \
  --billing-scope <subscription-id> \
  --term P1Y \
  --quantity 4

data.text: A **savings plan** is usually the better fit for App Service and Functions because it commits to a spend rate per hour across a family of compute rather than to a specific SKU — so you can change size and region without losing the discount.

Reservations are a bet on capacity you will definitely use. Committing to your peak means paying for the peak around the clock, and if the architecture changes (scale-to-zero, new SKU, region move) an unused reservation is money already spent and non-refundable. Covering p05 usage captures most of the discount at almost no risk.

cards.title: Savings plan (compute)
cons: You pay the commitment even at zero usage
Compute only, not storage or bandwidth
